STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of roasted or fried Brussels sprouts on a white square plate, photographed from directly above (near top-down view).

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 22 cm across its width. Area ≈ 22 × 22 × 0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 410 cm². Using a circle-equivalent diameter of ~22 cm gives 380 cm²; I use ~400 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: About 15 individual crispy, browned Brussels sprouts (halved or whole, with some charred edges). No visible sauce or oil pool.

STEP 4 - Area: The sprouts cluster in a pile covering roughly 12% of the plate area (about 48 cm²).

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile height averages about 2 cm for the outer envelope (sprouts are roughly 2–2.5 cm across, stacked in places). 48 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 96 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut/whole vegetable bulk density ~0.6 g/ml. 96 ml × 0.6 ≈ 58 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Roasted Brussels sprouts cooked with a little oil, about 50 kcal/100 g (fried/oil-roasted pushes this up slightly; I use 55 kcal/100 g). 58 g × 0.55 ≈ 32 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Fifteen small sprouts at roughly 3–4 g each is about 50–60 g, which matches. A small side portion of about 60 g and ~30–35 kcal is plausible.
